first_impression.reaction: I searched 'crete wedding packages' on the train. The second sentence tells me what's usually in one and the third tells me where they differ, so I have my answer before the first scroll. The four takeaways are short and clear. I'd skim the takeaways, jump to the all-inclusive question and what's left out, screenshot the quote checklist, then check the FAQ.

journey.quote: Most bundle a ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a chosen space.
journey.reaction: Second sentence and there's my answer. No wading through fluff.

journey.quote: Guest rooms, minimum stays, the reception and outside suppliers are where Crete packages differ most, so ask about each one in writing.
journey.reaction: This is the bullet I'd actually remember. Tells me where the catches are.

journey.quote: Euphoria's Elxi option serves sparkling wine and a single-tier cake with sugared almonds for up to 10 guests, on the beach or poolside.
journey.reaction: Fine, but then Elxi comes up again further down with another long list. Feels like I'm reading the same hotel twice.

journey.quote: On the day, it covers two witnesses if needed, a ceremony set-up with seasonal flowers, a bouquet and boutonniere, a pre-recorded playlist, champagne while getting ready and a short fireworks display, followed by champagne breakfast in bed.
journey.reaction: This whole section is hotel after hotel of long item lists. On my phone I can't hold one in my head long enough to compare it with the next. I start thumbing past.

journey.quote: Its 2025 to 2026 brochure package, The Basics, lists the ceremony, coordination services, photography, videography, Chiavari chairs, chair covers, table decoration, bridal party flowers and a wedding arch, with a wedding coordinator preparing the details.
journey.reaction: 2025 to 2026 in there. So this is current, which answers my 'is this still true' worry.

journey.section: Are Crete wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: Rarely, in the sense most couples mean.
journey.reaction: Heading is my next question word for word, and the answer is the first word. Perfect.

journey.section: Are Crete wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: At Grecotel Amirandes, "All Inclusive" appears as a hotel meal plan, not a wedding package.
journey.reaction: Ha, that's exactly the trap I'd have fallen into. Useful.

journey.quote: Out of the Blue settles registry office fees inside its Civil and Orthodox packages, so the same question has two different answers on one island.
journey.reaction: Good concrete example of why I need to ask. Short and skimmable.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: Nana Princess recommends evening ceremonies, because high-summer temperatures can reach 35 degrees C, with ceremonies from 6.30pm to 8pm in July and August.
journey.reaction: Didn't think about heat at all. The bold checklist around this is what I'd screenshot and bookmark the page for.

journey.quote: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only CNIs issued in their own country, so ask whether yours needs an apostille too.
journey.reaction: All Australian paperwork. Not my country, so I skip it. Fair enough, but it's a long stretch that isn't for me.

journey.quote: Usually not, and some require it.
journey.reaction: Short answer first, then the examples. That's how an FAQ should read.

journey.quote: No. The Elounda SA brochure states that symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised in Greece.
journey.reaction: Clear yes or no. Exactly what I'd want from a quick check.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Crete wedding package cost? Even a ballpark. There's no price anywhere.
Does Wedded Wonderland help couples outside Australia, or is this only for Australians?
If I only read one thing, which venue suits a couple-only elopement best?

turn_offs_found.quote: On the day, it covers two witnesses if needed, a ceremony set-up with seasonal flowers, a bouquet and boutonniere, a pre-recorded playlist, champagne while getting ready and a short fireworks display, followed by champagne breakfast in bed.
turn_offs_found.why: 'What Crete venue packages include' runs as seven long venue-by-venue blocks of item lists. On a phone I can't compare them side by side; I'd want a one-line summary per venue (ceremony type, guest numbers, stay required or not) before the full list, or a small table.

turn_offs_found.quote: Euphoria's Elxi option serves sparkling wine and a single-tier cake with sugared almonds for up to 10 guests, on the beach or poolside.
turn_offs_found.why: Euphoria's tiers are described in 'Types', again in 'What Crete venue packages include' and again in the FAQ. The repeats make the page feel longer than it needs to be when I'm scrolling for an answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit
turn_offs_found.why: Coming straight after two Australian-only sections, this makes me think the service isn't for someone in Singapore, so I'm less likely to bookmark or come back.

would_share_with: My engaged friend collecting quotes; I'd send her the 'How to compare two Crete quotes like for like' checklist

cta_reaction.why: I'm just looking, not ready to talk to anyone. No pop-ups or walls, so no complaints, and I'd bookmark before I'd book. The AUD and Australia framing also makes me unsure they'd take me.

top_3_changes: In 'What Crete venue packages include', open each venue with a one-line summary (ceremony types, guest numbers, stay required) before its full inclusion list, or add a short comparison table, so it can be skimmed on a phone.
Cut the repeated Euphoria tier details so each tier is described in full once, with the other mentions kept to a short cross-reference.
Phrase the AUD line in the CTA as a benefit for Australian couples rather than implying the service is only for Australians.
